I still remember only once that I carried out an investigation of an impact in one of the basements where people were collecting water, and it was a different kind of weapon used there. It had a hook-shaped nail back probably in the projectile, which it exploded, and it caused a lot of injuries. Also there were various calibres of rifles and machine-guns and anti-aircraft guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Right. For the moment, I want to stick to the rifle and machine-gun incidents that you investigated. When you were working on such investigations, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: The United Nations had a very elaborate system already in place. We had our headquarters in the PTT building, where a duty officer was there and, of course, a SMO, senior military observer, from Norway. He was a lieutenant-colonel, Mr. Pilan [phoen], if I am right in pronunciation. I don't know. And then we had our teams, as I have already mentioned, on Serb side and also on the BiH side, the government side. Along with that, at the headquarters, they had a liaison officer from warring factions and also a liaison officer from the troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just one moment, Mr. Butt, I'm sorry to interrupt you. I wanted to concentrate on your investigations involving, as you said, rifle and machine-guns and, let's say, small arms fire. What was your role when you undertook those investigations?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Right. Your Honours, I was supposed to -- on the instruction of headquarters or any information - because I wanted to give the system on how we were working anyway - received from the police or from troops deployed on the ground with the conformation from the headquarters, we would visit the site. And we used to investigate, if it was possible, what are the casualties, death or injured, direction of fire, calibre of fire, type of weapons used. And I make clear here, sir, that we used to only confirm the casualties which we could see in the hospital, if they were not there present on the ground, or in the accommodation. We only confirmed the casualties which we had met or we had seen physically. If we had not seen any casualty, physically, we would not confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you say, "direction of fire, calibre of fire, type of weapon used," was that ultimately to -- ultimately to enable you to determine where the shots had come from?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Yes. Mostly, it was possible, but sometime it was not possible because of the lack of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, sticking again with sniper fire or small-arms fire, do you recall an incident on the 15th of April in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: 15th of April, I believe this was a day when a French soldier was killed in front of Holiday Inn, and I along with another UNMO and an interpreter visited the site and investigated. And this was a day I remember vividly that once we went there, we were told it was a civilian, because I was not supposed to carry out investigation in case any UNPROFOR troop casualty is involved. When we reached there, though the body had already been removed as we were told but the French, we come to know it was a French soldier, who had already been killed, working in a fork-lift and fixing anti-sniping screen. But once we reached there, certainly we came under fire and we remained; myself, my colleague the other UNMO, and interpreter for about one hour, one hour, 15 minutes under fire, and later on rescued from the site through the arrangement of my headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, if I were to show you a photograph of that area, would you be able to point out or mark where you went to undertake that investigation?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Yes. I should be able to, if I'm shown that photograph or some map or things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And before I do that, you said that the French soldier had been working in a fork-lift fixing an anti-sniping screen. Why was he fixing an anti-sniping screen?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: First, let me be clear, there were a few hot spots and the famous "Sniper Alley." This is the main road running west of the town to east; that is, from the airport to the old part of the town, passing between museum and Holiday Inn. And there were a few spots and there were permanently anti-sniping team of the concerned UNPROFOR battalion were deployed, fully armed in APC. And they were ready to fire back in case they see anyone sniping. And later on, as the things were being analysed and the arrangements were being improved, it was probably decided to erect anti-sniping screens as it would save the commuters from sniping, as it would obstruct the visibility of the potential sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You use the word "hot spot" to describe this area. During your time there, did you know or did you see reports that, you said commuters, but civilians being hit at that area.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Yes. It was quite common. And we had a lot of reports, and I had also investigated quite a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So who told you to go down to that area to do this investigation, firstly?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: It was from my headquarters. The duty officer that day asked me to send the patrol, and I along with another UNMO and interpreter went there, as it was in my area of responsibility. I visited the site and carried out the investigation and came under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I show the witness photograph 06171146?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that's 65 ter 2825.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, we're just waiting for the photograph to come on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, if you could keep it at that size for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you recognise that area, Mr. Butt?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Yes, quite a familiar area. It was the centre of responsibility of my area and a very hot spot, so I do remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see on that photograph where you were when you went to investigate that incident on the 15th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know how I have to point. Is this red button the cursor or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No. I'm going to get the court usher to provide you with a marker, and I'd like to you mark the place where you were and where you came under sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. This was the place where fork-lift was and anti-sniping screens were being fixed here. And behind the anti-sniping screens I, along with my other UNMO and interpreter, took the cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And how long were you under sniper fire for?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: I was under sniper's fire for about 1 hour, 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes. And I was constantly in touch with my headquarter because my soft-skin vehicle was parked somewhere here on the other side, somewhere here, on the green patch. And firing -- it was so much firing that we couldn't reach to our soft-skin vehicle as at this point there was already one French anti-sniping team comprising two APCs. Once firing started, they fled and then we had to take cover. And I still remember that during my transmission with the headquarter duty officer at PTT building, they point out that from where I was being fired upon the building I did make mention.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Right. I'm going to get to that in a moment. But just so this photograph is clear and your evidence is recorded properly, the X that you've marked, that's the area where your soft-skin vehicle was; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: In fact, on top of X there is a triangle kind of thing I was able to draw and that is point where vehicle was parked. Its door was open, driver door, and we were on this. Again, I am pointing out this was a time -- the area we were pinned down and behind the sniping screen. And also fork-lift was still standing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I just want you to -- where the X and the triangle is, can you just put a small V on the top of that.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And where you have indicated where you were under sniper fire, please put the letter B.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: B. And B is -- I -- is not at right place. It is little down, because those are already painted in red, so it will not be possible to draw B there. So it is a little on my side, towards the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's fine. Now, you told us a moment ago that you that you were able to point out from where you were being fired upon. Where were you being fired from -- fired upon from?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Should I point out the building or the direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, first say where you think you were being fired from.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: I was fired from this direction. This is an arrow, by the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was the height of the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Screen, about -- these were being fixed there. These were slabs, kind of things, and about six feet high, if I remember correctly, and these were two or three, because was being placed, if I can draw, in steps, one overlapping with each other, and then the third one, in steps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, may I just ask you not to mark on the photograph unless I instruct you, just so your evidence is properly recorded.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Right, sir. It was just to give you the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I understand. And that's helpful for the Court and I thank you. Now, were you able to see who was sniping at you?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Yes, I could make out from where the fire was coming. And same was reported to headquarter giving the details of the building which was on the other side of the river. That means under Serb control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what was that building?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Do you want me to point out on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: First answer the question: What was the name of the building.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you now mark where that building is in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you just put a M on the top of that building.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How did you know that the sniper fire was coming from that building?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT
utterances.text: Because I could see somebody moving in those windows of this building and then firing. Because it was not single shot. It was much more than that and spread over about one hour, 1 hour, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps this is the time to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes, it is. We'll adjourn until tomorrow at 2.15 when we will be in Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry, may I just have this photograph admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P222, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of February, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
